newsitem.title: USA: Nordstrom reports higher first-quarter profit.
newsitem.headline: Nordstrom reports higher first-quarter profit.

text.p: Nordstrom Inc. on Monday reported better-than-expected first-quarter profits, reflecting higher sales and better cost controls.

The upscale retailer earned a profit of $32.3 million, or 41 cents a share, in the three months ended April 30, a 25 percent rise from $25.9 million, or 32 cents, a year ago. Net sales grew 5.3 percent to $953.7 million from $906 million.
According to First Call, which tracks Wall Street earnings predictions, analysts had expected the company to report a profiit of 34 cents a share.
Nordstrom Chairman John Whitacre attributed the improvement to improved cost controls.

"While we have seen a modest rise in sales trends, we are encouraged by improvement in expense control and gross margins that contributed to increased earnings," he said. "We are beginning to see better results in several of our women's apparel departments.
"Store expansion into new market areas continues to be a major focus of our growth strategy,' Whitacre added. "At the same time, we are equally committed to increase sales in our existing stores."
